transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me, I really appreciate it. 

Um, I guess I'm here because... well, I'm a high school teacher, and I really do love my job, but I've been having this little issue with my focus. I hope I'm explaining this right, but... I'll sit down at my desk with a stack of my students' essays, or maybe a new curriculum document, and I fully intend to just get to work. But then, maybe ten minutes later, I'll realize I've just been staring at the exact same page the whole time. My mind will have wandered off, and I'll be thinking about three other completely different things, barely taking in whatever is right in front of me. 

I mean, I know everyone gets a little distracted sometimes, right? I'm sure it's somewhat normal, and I don't want to sound like I'm just complaining. But it's been slowing me down a bit, and I just want to make sure I'm doing the best job I can for my students. Does that make sense? Is that the sort of thing I should be bringing up?
Looking back at your life, do you remember struggling with this type of inattentiveness or difficulty focusing when you were a child, or is this something that has only started more recently?

Um, well... I guess it isn't exactly a new thing. I really don't want to make it sound like I was a bad student or anything, because I always tried my best to behave and do what I was told! But, um, looking back... even in primary school, my report cards would usually say things like I was "bright but careless," or that I didn't finish my work unless I was closely supervised. Which, you know, sounds a bit worse than it probably was! 

And my parents... they were always finding these old worksheets just kind of crumpled up at the bottom of my backpack that I had completely forgotten to hand in. I always felt terrible about it when they found them, because I never meant to be messy or forgetful, it just sort of happened. 

Is that... is that the sort of childhood thing you're asking about? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information.

Aside from these struggles with focus, do you often find yourself feeling physically restless, like you have an internal motor that won't turn off, or do you frequently interrupt others when they are speaking?

Oh, um, no, not really. I mean, I'm a teacher, so I'm on my feet a lot during the day, but I don't feel... driven by a motor or anything like that. I'm actually pretty quiet, most people would probably say I'm on the calm side. 

And I really try hard to be a good listener! I know how frustrating it is when someone talks over you, so I always try to wait my turn. Sometimes I might get a little excited about a topic and jump in, but I think everyone does that now and then, right? I'd hate for anyone to think I was being rude or interrupting them on purpose. So, no, I wouldn't say I struggle with either of those things. Is that okay? I hope that helps narrow things down a bit.
Outside of your work, do you find that you frequently lose important items like your keys or phone, or have trouble keeping your personal schedule or household tasks organized?

Um, well... I guess I do misplace things sometimes. I mean, I try really hard to keep everything together, I really do! But, um... yeah, I suppose I do spend a fair amount of time hunting for things I need for the day. 

It's usually just silly little things, you know? Like my classroom keys, or my lesson notes... or my USB drive. Oh, and I help out with refereeing some of the sports games after school, so sometimes I'll be running around looking for my whistle or my penalty cards. And the funny thing is, I'll be so sure I just had them in my hand like, five minutes earlier! 

I know it sounds a bit disorganized, and I always feel so embarrassed when I have to ask my wife if she's seen my keys again. I really don't want to seem like I'm completely falling apart at home. I manage to get by, mostly! I just... I guess I do lose track of those little items more often than I'd like to admit. Does that sound like the kind of thing you're asking about? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.
Do you often find yourself avoiding or delaying starting tasks that require a lot of sustained mental effort, like grading those essays you mentioned?

Um, well... I wouldn't say I *avoid* them, exactly. I mean, I know grading essays is a huge part of my job, and I really do care about giving my students good feedback! I'd never want them to think I was just ignoring their hard work. 

But, um... I guess I do sometimes put it off a little bit? Like, I'll sit down at my desk with a stack of papers, and then I'll realize my desk is a bit messy, so I'll tidy that up first. And then maybe I need to reply to a few quick emails... and before I know it, it's getting late and I haven't actually started grading yet. 

I always get them done eventually, though! I might have to stay up a bit late to finish them right before they're due, but I really try my best not to let anyone down. I just... I suppose it can be a bit hard to just sit down and dive into something that takes that much focus all at once. Is that... does that make sense? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible teacher!
How much do these difficulties with focus and organization impact your day-to-day life or your performance at work, beyond just causing you a bit of extra stress?

Um, well... I guess they do impact things a little more than just stress. I mean, I really try to keep it all under control, I promise I do! I'd hate for you to think I'm just letting everything slide. 

But, um... at work, I guess the missed follow-through on some things has gotten a little noticeable. My department chair actually put me on a... a support plan. It sounds worse than it is, really! It's just to help me stay on track, but I was so embarrassed. I always want to be the kind of teacher they can rely on, you know? 

And at home... well, my wife is wonderful, she really is. But she's had to start taking over paying the bills and keeping track of our reminders and things. She said she just couldn't really count on me to remember them, which... which was hard to hear. I want to be a good partner, and I feel awful that she has to take on that extra burden because of me. 

So, I suppose it is affecting things a bit more than I'd like. I'm really hoping to get a better handle on it, though! I want to do better for my students and my wife. Does that... is that the kind of information you were looking for? I hope I'm explaining it alright.
When you are working on tasks like grading essays, do you find that you frequently make careless mistakes, such as missing typos or overlooking details in the students' work?

Um, well... I really try to be as thorough as I can when I'm grading. I know how important it is for the kids to get accurate feedback, and I'd hate for them to think I wasn't paying close attention to what they wrote. 

But, um... I guess I'm not really sure if I make *careless* mistakes, exactly. I mean, I might occasionally miss a small typo here or there, but I think everyone does that sometimes, right? Especially when you've been looking at the same prompt for the twentieth time. 

I really do my best to catch everything important, though! I wouldn't say I'm frequently overlooking major details or anything like that. I want to make sure I'm grading them fairly. Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't sound like I'm doing a bad job with their papers.
When you are in a meeting or a long conversation with someone, do you find that your mind drifts off and you lose track of what is being said, even if you are trying your best to listen?

Um, well... I really do try to be a good listener. I know how important it is to be present, especially when my wife is talking, or when we're in those long planning meetings at school. I always want people to feel heard and respected, you know?

But, um... I guess sometimes my mind does wander just a little bit? Like, I'll be looking right at the person, and I'm nodding and making eye contact, really trying to stay with them... but then they'll ask me what I think about something, and I realize I sort of... missed the actual point of what they just said. 

It's not that I don't care about what they're saying! I really do. It's just like my brain sort of takes a little detour without my permission. I usually try to piece it together from context clues so I don't seem rude. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible husband or a bad colleague. Does that... is that normal for people to do sometimes?
Do you often find that you have trouble finishing tasks like your lesson planning or household chores because you get sidetracked by other things before you can complete them?

Um, well... I really try my hardest to get everything done. I don't want you to think I'm just leaving things half-finished all over the place! I always want to be dependable, both at home and at school. 

But, um... I guess sometimes things do get a little... derailed? Like, if my department chair gives me three or four things to do after a meeting, I'm really good about jumping right in. I'll start the first one, and I usually get almost all the way through it! 

It's just that sometimes... well, the very last step sort of slips my mind. Like, I'll write up the whole document, but then I'll get distracted before actually sending the file. Or I'll plan out the whole week but forget to update the shared calendar or print the handouts. It usually just takes a quick reminder from someone and then I get it right done! I promise I'm not doing it on purpose to be difficult. I just get caught up in the next thing, I suppose. 

I hope that doesn't sound too awful. I really am trying to be more on top of those final details. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
